correctness.rationale: For a given word with k maps ×a and t−k maps ×b, the multiplier is a^k b^(t−k); the image of Z/(ab)^n is the uniform cyclic subgroup of cardinality (ab)^n/gcd((ab)^n,a^k b^(t−k))=a^((n−k)_+)b^((n−t+k)_+). Its centered CDF sawtooth has mean-subtracted variance 1/(12M²), so D=1/(M√12) exactly, including t=0 and M=1. Collapse means k≥n and t−k≥n, giving the exact finite-time binomial sum. For t=floor(2n+s√n), p_n=1/2+β/√n, triangular-array CLT gives (K_t−n)/√n⇒s/2+2β+Z/√2 and the complementary count gives s/2−2β−Z/√2. The continuous-mapping theorem on positive parts proves the claimed log profile. Indicator continuity away from Gaussian boundary proves the Bernoulli weak limit for s≥0; for s<0 collapse is impossible. Monotonicity of collapse yields τ limit |4β+√2Z|. At fixed p≠1/2 the minority selections arrive by a sum of n geometric waits, with mean n/q and variance n(1−q)/q²; at that time the other count exceeds n with probability tending to 1. None of the finite enumerations supplies the n→∞ step.
residual_risks: Requires coprime a,b and a common random map at each time applied to the whole grid; correlations across grid points are not independent map choices.
The limit concerns collapse to a point mass, not invariant Lebesgue mixing.
No assertion of strong joint path convergence beyond fixed s profile.
